title: Development of mouse anti-Ara h 1 and Ara h 3 IgE monoclonal antibodies for peanut allergy research
author: Waritani, Lomax, et al.
materials: CPE proteins were separated in a 10 % or 12 % SDS gel with or without 0.05 % 2-Mercaptoethanol (Sigma). To assess protein separation, the gel was stained with Coomassie brilliant blue R-250 (Sigma) according to the manufacturer's instructions. The separated proteins were transferred to a nitrocellulose membrane (Thermo Fisher, MA, USA). The membrane was then blocked with Casein/TBS and incubated with diluted anti-CPE mAbs at 4°C overnight. After washing the membrane with PBST, it was incubated with biotin-labeled anti-mouse IgE monoclonal antibodies (Chondrex) in Casein/TBS at RT for 2 hours. After washing the membrane with PBST, it was then incubated with HRP-labeled streptavidin (Chondrex) in Casein/TBS at RT for 30 minutes. The protein bands were visualized by adding TMB for immuno-blot (Thermo Fisher).

steps.title: Prepare crude peanut extract
steps.instruction: Extract, fractionate, and store peanut proteins for downstream use.

substeps.instruction: Manually grind raw peanuts with a coffee grinder to a fine powder.
Suspend powder in TBS buffer (65 mM Tris‑HCl, 1 mM EDTA, 1 mM PMSF, 200 mM NaCl, pH 8.3) at a 2:100 w/v ratio and stir 1 h at room temperature.
Filter the suspension through Grade GF/A filters (Whatman) and centrifuge the filtrate at 10,000 × g for 30 min at 4 °C.
Dialyze the supernatant against distilled water, then lyophilize the dialysate.
Dissolve the lyophilized powder in TBS buffer, add solid ammonium sulfate to reach 40 % saturation, and centrifuge at 30,000 × g for 30 min at 4 °C.
Collect the supernatant, increase ammonium sulfate to 70 % saturation, and centrifuge again at 30,000 × g for 30 min at 4 °C.
Resuspend the resulting pellet in TBS buffer, clarify by a final centrifugation, and store aliquots at –70 °C.
Determine protein concentration of each batch with the Pierce BCA kit (using BSA standard).

steps.title: Run SDS‑PAGE and immunoblot
steps.instruction: Separate CPE proteins, transfer to membrane, and detect IgE binding.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 10 % or 12 % SDS‑PAGE gel, adding 0.05 % 2‑Mercaptoethanol if reducing conditions are desired.
Load CPE samples, run electrophoresis, then stain the gel with Coomassie brilliant blue R‑250 according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Transfer separated proteins onto a nitrocellulose membrane (Thermo Fisher).
Block the membrane with Casein/TBS solution.
Incubate the blocked membrane with diluted anti‑CPE monoclonal antibodies at 4 °C overnight.
Wash the membrane with PBST (PBS + Tween‑20).
Incubate with biotin‑labeled anti‑mouse IgE monoclonal antibodies (Chondrex) in Casein/TBS at room temperature for 2 h.
Wash again with PBST.
Incubate with HRP‑labeled streptavidin (Chondrex) in Casein/TBS at room temperature for 30 min.
Wash with PBST and develop the blot by adding TMB substrate (Thermo Fisher) to visualize protein bands.

steps.title: Prepare anti‑CPE IgE affinity column
steps.instruction: Couple monoclonal antibody to gel, block, bind CPE, and elute bound proteins.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve mouse anti‑CPE IgE mAb 2G11G7 in 3 ml PBS to a concentration of 2 mg ml⁻¹.
Mix the antibody solution with 1 ml ALD‑Actigel and ALD‑coupling solution; incubate overnight at 4 °C to covalently attach the antibody to the gel.
Block any remaining reactive sites by incubating the antibody‑bound gel with 0.1 M Tris and ALD‑coupling buffer, then wash the gel with 0.1 M TBS (pH 8.0).
Pass CPE prepared in 0.1 M TBS (pH 8.0) through the column; wash the column with the same TBS buffer to remove unbound proteins.
Elute the bound CPE fraction using 0.1 M glycine‑HCl buffer (pH 2.6).
Dialyze the eluate against 0.1 M TBS (pH 8.0) to neutralize and remove glycine‑HCl.
